$comment: Mazda 20B-REW (three-rotor sequential twin-turbo, Eunos Cosmo JCESE, 1990-1995). Researched 2026-09-27 to 2026-09-29. Primary sources: Mazda’s 1990 Eunos Cosmo brochure and 1997 Mazda Motorsports (US) competition parts catalogue, Mazda’s RE vehicle album; the goo-net, Car Sensor and carview catalogues; Mazdatrix and FD-swap vendors for the swap hardware. Mazda publishes much less on the 20B than the 13B: no port timing, weight, dimensions, redline, injector flow or turbo model was found in a Mazda document, and the firing order is estimated. Rotor geometry is the 13B’s (shared rotor and rotor-housing part numbers). Displacement and rpm follow the rotary convention in docs/decisions.md.

firingOrder.method: The rotors are 120° apart on the eccentric shaft, so one rotor fires every 120° of shaft rotation (http://www.ausrotary.com/viewtopic.php?t=26822; https://www.msextra.com/doc/ms1extra/MS_Extra_Ignition_Hardware_Manual.htm; forum and ECU documentation, no Mazda document). Which rotor follows rotor 1 isn’t printed in any source that could be read: rx7club.com threads, blocked from here, are summarised by search engines as 1-2-3 for most 20Bs and 1-3-2 for some. 1-2-3 is stored as a placeholder; the even 120° spacing, which is what the sound and airflow need, is sourced.

dryWeight.method: No Mazda figure. The published numbers don’t share a basis: 260 lb (118 kg) “bare” (Paul Lamar, rotary aviation list) and 350 kg “with manifolds” (DRIFTED, copied by two other sites, and hard to reconcile with a 13B at about 155 kg). Estimated from the 13B-REW’s 155 kg (with turbos and manifolds, itself estimated) plus a third rotor (about 4.1 kg, Mazda Motorsports catalogue), a third rotor housing and a second intermediate housing (a stock 13B-REW intermediate housing weighs 25.9 lb, 11.7 kg, per Racing Beat), and a longer shaft, pan and manifolds: about +30 kg, so 185 kg, roughly +/-20 kg.

length.method: Placeholder from DRIFTED (drifted.com/20b-engine, “with accessories”, unsourced and nearly identical to the figure it gives for Mazda’s 13G race engine). No Mazda or specialist figure was found. For scale: a 13BT measures 19 in (483 mm) pulley to back of block (AusRotary), and the 20B adds one 80 mm rotor housing and one intermediate housing.

width.method: Placeholder from DRIFTED (drifted.com/20b-engine, “with accessories”, unsourced). No Mazda or specialist figure was found.

height.method: Placeholder from DRIFTED (drifted.com/20b-engine, “with accessories”, unsourced). The stock intake is too tall for an FD bonnet (FD swap vendors).

sources.note: REbyKenichiYamamoto-1981.pdf PDF page 18 = book p.12, section 2.1.2 PARALLEL TROCHOID CURVE: In the actual rotary engine, the curve used for the inner surface of its rotor housing is the trochoid given by Eq. (2.4) that has been moved outward in parallel by a constant amount a. The purpose of this is to form the top of the apex seal in a circular section in the radius a ... This curve is closely approximate to the trochoid drawn with the generating radius R increased by the amount of the parallel transfer a. In ordinary calculation, a sufficient accuracy for practical use can be obtained by substituting R+a for the generating radius R in Eq. (2.4).

In such a case, the volume of the working chamber can be approximately calculated in practically sufficient accuracy by taking R1=R+a and R2=R+a', as follows: ... The stroke volume V_H becomes V_H' = √3 e(2R1+R2)b ... (2.30)

rotorHousing.note: aluminium-alloy rotor housings with SIP steel trochoid insert (same parts family as the FC 13B turbo). No 20B-specific material statement. The 20B shares FC 13B turbo rotor-housing part numbers (catalogue), and Mazda's album bar for 1986-2007 applies to all production rotaries of that period. Aluminium itself is from Yamamoto (general) and Coleman (13B-REW) only.

sources.note: We offer a series of Aircraft Grade A356 aluminum alloy side housings to replace many of the heavier, cast iron stock assemblies found on all 1974 and later 12A, 13B, 20B, and 13G engines.

sideHousings.note: special cast iron with nitrided sliding surfaces: front, two intermediate (one thick, one thin) and rear housings. The Mazdatrix 'HOUSING REAR 20B, ALUMINUM' (SKU 11072) is an aftermarket Racing Beat part ('Sorry, Racing Beat has discontinued this item'; 'Flame Sprayed Aluminum Rear Side Housings 20B – Racing Beat Exclusive'), cast in A356, T-6 heat-treated and flame/plasma-sprayed. It is not the stock part; the same text says the stock housings are cast iron with a nitride surface. Housing count (4 side housings) is from engine-20b-2 (1997 catalogue and Mazdatrix).

rotors.method: Only Mazda’s general engineering text (Yamamoto, Rotary Engine, 1981) names the rotor material, nodular graphite cast iron, for Mazda’s production rotaries; no document for this engine says it (https://www.foxed.ca/rx7manual/manuals/97CatComp.pdf; https://www.foxed.ca/rx7manual/manuals/REbyKenichiYamamoto-1981.pdf).

eccentricShaft.method: Two pieces joined at the centre by a taper joint with a key (Motor-Fan, a minkara owner rebuild and Mazda centre-key part NF01-11-D19 via Mazdatrix: https://mazdatrix.com/product/3r-keyway-center-shaft-center-key/; https://minkara.carview.co.jp/userid/140048/car/240911/742606/note.aspx; https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/019cba459d3c0a1df24be3dd950065ac4113c8c8; https://www.foxed.ca/rx7manual/manuals/REbyKenichiYamamoto-1981.pdf; https://www.motorverso.com/20b-engine/); no source says whether a centre bolt is also used. Forged steel is from Mazda’s general text (Yamamoto 1981), not confirmed for the 20B. The shaft has its own centre main bearing and centre stationary gear.
